sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Legal Basis**: EIA Notification 2006 issued under Section 3 of the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**.
• **Core Objective**: To integrate environmental concerns into the developmental process at the planning stage.
• **Institutional Framework**: Projects are appraised by the **Expert Appraisal Committee (EAC)** at the Central level and **State Level Expert Appraisal Committee (SEAC)** at the State level.
• **Key Metric**: The **Environmental Clearance (EC)** is the final mandatory approval required for project commencement.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Projects of national importance; high pollution potential.
Small-scale projects; often exempted from public consultation.

items.definition: Determining whether a project requires an EIA and the level of assessment needed.
Defining the Terms of Reference (ToR) to identify key environmental issues to be studied.
A mandatory process to hear the concerns of local affected people; results are recorded in the minutes.
Detailed scrutiny of the EIA report by the EAC/SEAC to recommend grant or rejection of EC.

items.title: Major Applications
items.content:
• **PARIVESH Portal**: Single-window integrated environmental management system for online submission and tracking of EC applications.
• **Post-Clearance Monitoring**: Compliance reports submitted by project proponents to Regional Offices of MoEFCC.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Poor quality of EIA reports (outsourced to consultants), lack of public participation, and post-clearance monitoring failures.
• **Solutions**: Independent EIA audits, strengthening the National Green Tribunal (NGT), and mandatory social impact assessments.

items.title: Mnemonic for EIA Stages
items.content:
• **Phrase**: 'SS-P-A-D' (Stop, See, Plan, Act, Decide).
• **Decoded**: Screening -> Scoping -> Public Consultation -> Appraisal -> Decision.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Public Consultation' as mandatory for ALL projects. It is NOT mandatory for Category B2 projects.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Procedural Democracy' when discussing the importance of Public Consultation in EIA.

keyTakeaways: EIA is a statutory requirement under the EPA 1986, not a constitutional mandate.
The MoEFCC is the final authority for Category A projects, while SEIAA handles Category B.
Public consultation is a critical check-and-balance mechanism for local environmental justice.
